reason: EXAMPLE (the common case) — one specific submission: address + chain + registry. Found already tagged on etherscan 2026-07-16. Scoped to submissions so a future removal of this item still earns its removal reward. Fields: registry is one of addressTags | tokens | domains; scope is one of submissions | removals | atq | all (default all).

EXAMPLE — non-EVM works too: chain is the CAIP-2 reference, i.e. the chain id for EVM (1, 137, 8453, 42161, ...) or the genesis-hash reference for Solana, exactly as it appears in the Chain column of the fetch/removals CSVs.

EXAMPLE (blanket ban) — chain and registry omitted = this address matches on EVERY chain and in EVERY registry; scope all = never rewarded again, neither as submission nor as removal. Use for spam / bad-faith addresses.
EXAMPLE — a removal that should not be rewarded (e.g. remover cleared their own bogus submission). Applied before dedupe, so an earlier legitimate removal of the same item still counts.
EXAMPLE — ATQ entries match by itemID only (ATQ rows have no tagged address). Take the Item ID from the <runId>_atq_registered.csv / <runId>_atq_absent.csv reports.

EXAMPLE — itemID also works for the three main registries when you want to pin one exact Curate item instead of an address; both the bare itemID and the <itemID>@<registry-address> id form match. No scope = all. Every entry MUST have a reason and at least one of tagAddress / itemID; matching is case-insensitive; an entry that matches nothing prints a WARNING; a malformed file aborts the run.
